title: React Module 03 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of JSX syntax, expressions, attributes, fragments, children, JSX versus HTML, and text safety.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A JavaScript syntax extension for describing UI

questions.explanation: JSX lets React developers write markup-like UI descriptions in JavaScript.

questions.prompt: Which rule applies when a component returns JSX?
questions.explanation: A component must return a single root element or Fragment.

questions.prompt: Which JSX attribute should you use instead of HTML `class`?
questions.explanation: JSX uses `className` because `class` is a JavaScript keyword-related DOM property naming concern.

questions.prompt: Which JSX attribute should a label use instead of HTML `for`?
questions.explanation: React JSX uses `htmlFor` for label associations.

questions.prompt: Which can be placed inside JSX curly braces? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: JSX braces accept expressions, not statements such as a raw `if`.

questions.prompt: Fragments let a component return adjacent elements without adding an extra DOM wrapper.
questions.explanation: Fragments group children in React without creating an extra DOM node.

questions.prompt: How do inline styles work in JSX?

options.text: Pass a JavaScript object, such as `style={{ color: "red" }}`
Pass a CSS string only, such as `style="color: red"`
Inline styles are impossible in JSX

questions.explanation: The JSX `style` prop expects an object with camelCased property names.

questions.prompt: Which values does React usually skip rendering as visible text? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: React ignores booleans, null, and undefined as children, while strings render as text.
